The structural unification maps discrete product options (Perun, Foxbat) and continuous scaling variables (MW, M2) into a constrained optimization manifold, governed by temporal escalation vectors and strict array-length computational boundaries.

The GB Master document functions as a rigorous initialization protocol for a massive, multi-variable capital expenditure simulation. Mathematically, we derive three core operators from the provided excerpts. First, the Configuration Space Projection Operator isolates the discrete degrees of freedom—specifically the Perun, Foxbat, and Zilla variants. This acts as a selection matrix, projecting the infinite continuum of theoretical data center designs onto a finite, vendor-approved subspace. Once the iGMP (Issued for General Mechanical Permit) milestone is reached, this projection becomes rigid, mathematically freezing the basis vectors to prevent scope creep.

Second, the Temporal Escalation Kernel introduces a time-dependence to the static cost estimates. By anchoring to the Construction Agreement Execution Date and applying a monthly escalation period, we generate a continuous cost trajectory. This is not merely linear interpolation; it assumes an underlying stochastic process governing labor and material inflation, discretized into monthly steps for accounting purposes.

Third, the Computational Boundary Constraint reveals the finite nature of the simulation environment. The explicit mention of 'Array Formula Length' (3000 for GC, 500 for GR) indicates a hard ceiling on the dimensionality of the Work Breakdown Structure (OneWBS) that can be processed simultaneously. This creates a bottleneck regime: if the physical complexity of the build requires more than 3000 distinct tracking nodes, the mathematical model must either truncate data or aggregate nodes, introducing approximation errors.

The duality here lies between the physical reality of the construction site (continuous, chaotic, evolving) and the digital twin represented by the GB Master (discrete, bounded, locked). Failure modes emerge precisely at the interface of these dualities: when physical delays force a modification to a locked iGMP configuration, or when the sheer volume of sub-contractor tasks breaches the 3000-element array limit, causing the estimation engine to crash or return invalid '#REF!' states.
